identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips

scan.summary: This is the facility's written food safety plan required under FSMA's Preventive Controls rule (21 CFR 117), covering ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips produced at the Salem plant. The plan identifies biological, physical, and allergen hazards; specifies preventive controls such as cooking time and temperature, cooling parameters, sanitation, allergen labeling, and metal detection; and describes monitoring, corrective actions, verification, and supply-chain supplier verification procedures.
scan.freshness_note: This plan is current as of its effective date of May 12, 2025, and is now over 16 months old (today is September 28, 2026). The plan remains in effect unless it has been superseded or updated. No review or renewal deadline is stated in the document itself; plans remain valid until revised.

conditions.title: Cook beans to minimum 212°F for at least 60 minutes
conditions.condition_ref: Section 4, Cooking of beans preventive control
conditions.evidence_expected: Cook logs documenting internal temperature and time at start and end of each batch, measured with calibrated probe thermometer

conditions.title: Cool cooked beans from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours, then to 41°F within 4 additional hours
conditions.evidence_expected: Cooling logs documenting temperatures at 2 hours and 6 hours using blast chiller

conditions.title: Sanitation of food-contact surfaces before each production run and between products
conditions.evidence_expected: ATP swab results (pass required before start-up) and Listeria spp. swabs from 10 sites weekly in zone 1 and 2

conditions.title: Environmental monitoring for Listeria
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly Listeria spp. environmental swab results from 10 designated sites

conditions.title: Allergen label review and product scheduling
conditions.evidence_expected: Label logs verified against formulation sheets; production scheduled with hummus items last, followed by ATP swab verification before next non-sesame product

conditions.title: Metal detection of every sealed tub
conditions.evidence_expected: Metal detector test records using three test pieces (2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless) at start-up, every two hours, and end of run

conditions.title: Finished product testing for Listeria monocytogenes
conditions.evidence_expected: Monthly test results for Listeria monocytogenes from accredited laboratory

conditions.title: Probe thermometer calibration
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly calibration records in ice water and boiling water

conditions.title: Records retention
conditions.evidence_expected: All named records (cook log, cooling log, sanitation ATP swabs, metal detector tests, label logs, corrective action log) kept at Salem plant for at least two years

expected_missing.title: Recall plan
expected_missing.why: 21 CFR 117.126(e) requires a written recall plan as part of the food safety plan; this document does not contain a recall plan section
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.126(e) specifies recall plan must be included in food safety plan

expected_missing.title: Chemical hazard analysis
expected_missing.why: The hazard analysis section (section 3) lists only biological, physical, and allergen hazards; chemical hazards are not explicitly addressed though the plan may rely on supplier controls
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.126(a)(1) requires identification of known or reasonably foreseeable chemical hazards; minimal discussion of pesticide residues, cleaning chemical contamination, or other chemical hazards

expected_missing.title: Allergen cross-contact control for bean dips
expected_missing.why: The plan addresses sesame allergen from tahini but does not detail controls for cross-contact of products made with or without tahini beyond 'product scheduling with hummus items last'
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.80(b) requires allergen controls to prevent cross-contact in facilities with multiple products

expected_missing.title: Validation of preventive controls
expected_missing.why: The plan does not describe validation studies or literature references supporting the cook and cool critical parameters or sanitation monitoring effectiveness
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.165(a) requires validation that preventive controls will be effective; monitoring results (section 7) mentions testing but not documented validation

expected_missing.title: Biological/chemical contaminant testing of incoming ingredients
expected_missing.why: The supply-chain program relies on supplier audit certificates and certificates of analysis but does not specify what tests suppliers must conduct or what tolerances apply
expected_missing.basis: Common practice for RTE hummus/dips due to Salmonella and Listeria risks in legumes and sesame

expected_missing.title: Intentional adulteration/food defense plan
expected_missing.why: No food defense or intentional adulteration prevention procedures are described, though 21 CFR 121 applies to human food facilities
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 121.1 requires food defense preventive measures; not addressed in this plan

expected_missing.title: Sanitation SOP
expected_missing.why: The preventive control specifies ATP and Listeria swab results but does not detail the written sanitation procedures, frequency, and responsibility assignments beyond 'before each production run'
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.10(b)(1) requires written sanitation procedures; this plan does not include or reference a separate sanitation SOP

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the identity and structure of this document. It is clearly a food safety plan prepared under FSMA's Preventive Controls rule. The hazard analysis is reasonably comprehensive for ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips, with appropriate identification of biological (vegetative pathogens, spore-formers, Listeria), physical (metal), and allergen (sesame) hazards. The preventive controls and critical limits are technically sound and appropriately matched to the hazards. Monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and verification activities are all described. The PCQI is identified and trained. Moderate confidence that the plan is fully compliant: the plan is missing a written recall plan (a required element under 21 CFR 117.126(e)), does not provide validation evidence for critical limits, does not explicitly address chemical hazards, and does not include a food defense plan (required under 21 CFR 121). The supply-chain section is sparse on detail regarding what tests suppliers must conduct. The plan's reliance on third-party audit certificates for supplier approval is reasonable but the specifics of supplier verification (what standards, what testing) are not detailed. The monitoring frequency for Listeria (weekly environmental swabs, monthly product testing) is appropriate for an RTE product with a 45-day shelf life; this aligns with FDA guidance on Listeria control. The plan does not describe a challenge testing or shelf-life study to validate that Listeria will not exceed regulatory limits during the 45-day shelf life, though monthly testing provides real-time verification.

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.
3. Hazard analysis

tahini contact with bean dips made without
tahini

5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
